claims.claim: The visible L1 gold records for the reference contexts uniformly report oral bioavailability values at or above 33%, with most in the 70–100% range: baclofen 73–86%, ciprofibrate ~90%, desvenlafaxine 80.5%, seletracetam >90%, ezetimibe 35–60%, doxercalciferol 41 ± 18%, and levodopa formulations 63.6–99%. No transferable direct low-F record is present.

The query is a zwitterionic aminocephalosporin with an alpha-amino-p-hydroxyphenylacetamido side chain and a 3-(1H-1,2,3-triazol-5-ylthio)methyl group. Despite very low logD and full ionization, the prior explicitly notes that beta-lactams can be absorbed via peptide transporters, and the high-F amino-acid-like oral drugs in the evidence support carrier-mediated oral absorption despite polarity.
The low chloramphenicol F values in malnourished children are disease-state observations and are not transferable to the query's normal oral absorption.

The low-F disease-state chloramphenicol records are not applicable to normal oral absorption of the query.
content.decision_summary: The physicochemical prior is low because of extreme polarity and ionization, but the visible L1 gold records uniformly support high oral bioavailability for the relevant amino-acid-like oral drugs, and the query is an oral aminocephalosporin with a known carrier-mediated absorption pathway. No affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F < 20%, so the better-supported prediction is high, with moderate confidence due to indirect transfer.
